correctness.rationale: For each n-tree T, law at census depth k is the exact integer induced-edge histogram H_T,k(j)/binom(n,k). For forests, induced components equal k-j, so full depths reindex the subgraph-component polynomial. Exhaustive proof enumerates all unlabeled trees n<=10 inductively by all leaf attachments and canonical center-rooted AHU codes; each graph is generated and duplicate isomorphism types merged. Directly counting all 2^n subsets gives complete H_T,k histograms, not a partial sample. Independently computed via networkx nonisomorphic_trees and separate subset enumeration: numbers of shapes n=4..10 equal 2,3,6,11,23,47,106. Individual sufficient depths are n4:{3}, n5:{3,4}, n6:{4}, n7:{4,5}, n8:{5}; for n9 all seven individual depths fail with collision counts k=2..8 [1081,117,10,1,1,7,96], and exactly five sufficient depth pairs {4,6},{5,6},{5,7},{6,7},{6,8}. At n10 the complete set of depths has one known collision pair. The proof is a rigorous bounded complete census n<=10, not an infinite classification.

originality.rationale: Tittmann–Averbouch–Makowsky 2008/2011 define and study the full subgraph-component polynomial, showing uniqueness for tree orders <=9 and an indistinguishable pair at n=10. Those prior global results do not imply that one exact fixed-cardinality slice suffices through n8 or which pairs of slices suffice at n9. The delimited new theorem is the exact cardinality-sampling design and single-slice collision profile, not the prior full-polynomial ten-tree counterexample.

The theorem is strictly n<=10 and assumes the full ideal exact sampling distribution known; finite observations/noise or unknown n are outside scope.
